original_value: AbstractThe boomerang attack, introduced by Wagner in 1999, is a cryptanalysis technique against block ciphers based on differential cryptanalysis. In particular it takes into consideration two differentials, one for the upper part of the cipher and one for the lower part, and it exploits the dependency of these two differentials. At Eurocrypt’18, Cid et al. introduced a new tool, called the Boomerang Connectivity Table (BCT), that permits to simplify this analysis. Next, Boura and Canteaut introduced an important parameter for cryptographic S-boxes called boomerang uniformity, that is the maximum value in the BCT. Very recently, the boomerang uniformity of some classes of permutations (in particular quadratic functions) have been studied by Li, Qu, Sun and Li, and by Mesnager, Tang and Xiong. In this paper we further study the boomerang uniformity of some non-quadratic differentially 4-uniform functions. In particular, we consider the case of the Bracken-Leander cubic function and three classes of 4-uniform functions constructed by Li, Wang and Yu, obtained from modifying the inverse functions.

result.paraphrase: Abstract The boomerang attack, first introduced by Wagner in 1999, is a differential-cryptanalysis method for block ciphers. It considers two distinct differentials—one for the upper cipher part and one for the lower part—and exploits the dependence between them. At Eurocrypt 2018, Cid et al. proposed a new tool, the Boomerang Connectivity Table (BCT), which simplifies this analysis. Boura and Canteaut then defined an important cryptographic S-box parameter called boomerang uniformity, namely the maximum entry in the BCT. More recently, Li, Qu, Sun and Li, as well as Mesnager, Tang and Xiong, studied the boomerang uniformity of certain permutation classes, especially quadratic functions. In this paper, we further investigate the boomerang uniformity of some non-quadratic differentially 4-uniform functions, focusing in particular on the Bracken-Leander cubic function and three classes of 4-uniform functions constructed by Li, Wang and Yu by modifying inverse functions.
